title: ByteLadder: Prompt-Conditioned Progressive Precision for ProMixed KV Caches
hook: ByteLadder adds no action-value network and no counterfactual forward pass at serving time: it reuses ProMixed GQA scores to place independently addressable residual segments under the same exact KV-byte ceiling. The claim is that this strictly leaner runtime axis can outperform uniform-format ProMixed on held-out task categories because precision becomes a byte-by-byte promotion decision rather than a method-wide setting.
hook_shape_rationale: This is counter-intuitive minimalism: relative to a learned per-action router, ByteLadder adds zero model parameters and zero serving-time teacher passes while retaining a fixed three-profile lookup and one heap traversal. A surprising-empirical hook was also viable, but it was rejected because the direction of the held-out LongBench gain is the falsifiable result, whereas the sharper admission-test fact is the strict reduction in online learned machinery.

gap_closure.gap: No retrieved paper tests whether all retained regions in one request must share the same representation and retention rule rather than treating that inherited method-wide uniformity as necessary.
gap_closure.how_closed: Closed by encoding every nonmandatory historical layer-block as an omittable prefix of independently aligned, exactly charged residual extents and promoting different blocks through P4, P8, or lossy 16-code-bit P16 according to task-conditioned positive value per allocator byte. Mandatory FP16 recent-window and sink bytes are charged first; requests whose mandatory footprint already exceeds the ceiling are reported infeasible rather than claimed feasible.

gap_closure.gap: No retrieved frontier leaf closes the gap between offline model-level sensitivity and prompt-specific evidence strongly enough to preserve accuracy across task shifts while keeping selection overhead inside the serving deadline.
gap_closure.how_closed: Closed by retrieving three offline task-category promotion profiles from a canonical ProMixed prompt fingerprint and composing their layer-by-rung gains at inference, with entire task categories held out and no per-task parameter update.

core_mechanism: ByteLadder is a sequential pipeline over the same nonmandatory 16-token historical layer-blocks already scored by ProMixed. Let M be the allocator-reported bytes of mandatory FP16 recent-window and sink entries and B the request ceiling. If M>B, routing returns mandatory_budget_infeasible and makes no feasible-cache claim; if the historical set is empty or M=B, it returns the mandatory cache with B_used=M. Otherwise each FP16 key/value block X_lb is flattened to N_lb scalars and padded only in its final 64-scalar group. A successive codec maintains an FP32 residual r. For Qq(r), q in {4,8}, each group uses symmetric codes [-(2^(q-1)-1), 2^(q-1)-1]; if max(abs(r))=0 it stores a zero FP16 scale and zero codes, otherwise it stores the smallest finite positive FP16 scale s not below max(abs(r))/(2^(q-1)-1), applies round-to-nearest-even to r/s, and needs no clipping. The decoded segment is s times its code and the next residual is formed in FP32. Apply q1=Q4(X_lb), q2=Q4(X_lb-decode(q1)), and q3=Q8(X_lb-decode(q1)-decode(q2)). Modes are omit, P4={q1}, P8={q1,q2}, and P16={q1,q2,q3}; P16 means 16 dense code bits per scalar and remains lossy, so it is distinct from mandatory FP16. Each stage has the auditable groupwise infinity-norm rounding bound s/2. Every rung is an independent 64-byte-aligned extent with a 16-byte header and one 2-byte FP16 scale per 64-scalar group. For G=ceil(N_lb/64), incremental extent bytes are c1=c2=align64(16+34G) and c3=align64(16+66G); padding and headers are included, and a backend with larger extents substitutes its allocator-returned independent extent sizes before routing. Offline, each task category j, zero-based layer l, and rung u stores g_jlu, the mean full-cache teacher-forced suffix-KL reduction from that single promotion, plus centroid mu_j and diagonal variance. The twelve-value fingerprint averages, within zero-based strata floor(4l/L), normalized score entropy, pairwise top-k Jaccard, and kept-next margin. Entropy is zero for at most one scored block, Jaccard of two empty top-k sets is one, margin is zero when k=0 or no next block exists, and score ties break by block id. With J>0 profiles, retrieve R=min(3,J) centroids by (diagonal-whitened squared distance, category id), use the fixed 1e-4 variance floor, and compute softmax(-d/tau) with tau chosen from a finite positive validation grid; J=0 is a configuration error. The conditioned gain is ghat_lu=sum_j w_j g_jlu. For nonnegative ProMixed utility s_lb, create a rung item only when v_lbu=s_lb*ghat_lu is finite and positive, with priority v_lbu/c_lbu and deterministic max-heap key (priority,-l,-b,-u_index). Start with omit-to-P4. On each pop, discard an item whose independent extent exceeds remaining bytes and continue scanning; otherwise accept it, subtract its bytes, and expose only that block's next positive-valued rung. Thus precedence is strict, every fitting frontier is considered, the loop halts after at most three pops per block, and feasible B_used=M+sum(accepted c_lbu)<=B. After routing, materialize only accepted prefixes into their independent extents and decode them with fused residual-add attention kernels. Report actual KV allocation, conversion time, TTFT, throughput, and downstream outcomes end to end; no wall-clock hard guarantee is asserted.
core_mechanism_reasoning: The two gaps share a sequential dependency rather than one predictor: task-category profiles first condition layer-level promotion gains, and ProMixed prompt scores then place the resulting residual segments under the byte ceiling. An action-specific counterfactual predictor plus a two-resource program was rejected because it would need an unsupported hard latency cost model; a fixed Oaken-style threshold was rejected because it regresses to method-wide calibration, while fixed positional windows, attention-mass-only eviction, head sharing, paging, and offloading are occupied lineage nodes that do not supply prompt-conditioned precision promotion.
core_mechanism_steps:
1. Define the progressive codec and serialized layout beside the Qwen2.5-7B Re-Prefill path: input is the shape of each FP16 16-token layer-block X_lb; output is the q1:int4, q2:int4, q3:int8 residual-prefix specification, zero-scale rule, decoder, and independent aligned rung-cost functions c1,c2,c3. This step defines sizes but does not materialize all request segments.
2. Build the offline reference bank from LongBench training categories by running full-cache and single-rung promotion replays over teacher-forced suffixes; inputs are calibration prompts and frozen Qwen2.5-7B, and outputs are g_jlu tables, fingerprint centroids mu_j, and diagonal variances.
3. Split LongBench by entire task category, select tau only from a finite positive grid on validation categories, keep the variance floor fixed at 1e-4, and serialize the immutable bank; no task-specific weights are updated at serving time.
4. During prefill, retain ProMixed GQA score rows and compute the twelve-dimensional z and nonnegative s_lb using the specified n<=1, k=0, no-successor, and deterministic-tie conventions; if there are no historical blocks, bypass profiling and return the mandatory cache when feasible.
5. Require a nonempty bank, retrieve R=min(3,J) profiles with deterministic category-id tie breaks, compute w_j and ghat_lu, and emit positive finite omit-to-P4 items keyed by gain per independent exact incremental byte.
6. Read mandatory allocator bytes M and ceiling B. Return mandatory_budget_infeasible when M>B; return only mandatory data when M=B; otherwise run the deterministic heap, discarding a nonfitting frontier item but continuing to smaller items, and expose a successor only after predecessor acceptance. Output one mode per block and B_used=M+sum accepted bytes<=B.
7. Quantize from the prefill X_lb tensors and materialize only each accepted prefix into its independently aligned extents; output physical mixed-format KV pages and mode offsets whose allocator total equals the bytes charged in Step 6.
8. Decode P4, P8, or lossy 16-code-bit P16 prefixes with fused residual-add kernels before the existing attention dot product; output the ordinary attention result through unchanged remaining Qwen layers.
9. Log actual KV bytes, conversion time, TTFT, decode throughput, and downstream predictions for paired comparisons against uniform-format ProMixed, DynamicKV-style layer budgets, Oaken-style fixed calibration, and global-profile ByteLadder.
10. Run the profile-permutation negative control and oracle-category positive control at identical bytes and ProMixed scores; output the downstream causal test of profile conditioning.
falsification_prediction: On Qwen2.5-7B, hold out complete LongBench task categories from the reference bank and evaluate those categories plus Needle-in-a-Haystack at 5%, 10%, and 25% allocator-measured historical-KV byte ceilings against uniform-format ProMixed and global-profile ByteLadder, while reporting actual TTFT rather than enforcing a wall-clock claim. If ByteLadder works, held-out LongBench score and NIAH exact-match increase at the same or lower measured KV bytes, with the largest gain at 5% and 10%; P95 TTFT is a separately reported deployment outcome and may rise or fall. The single load-bearing variable is the prompt-conditioned promotion-gain table ghat_lu(z). As a negative control, randomly permute the association between profile centroids and their g_jlu tables while leaving ProMixed scores, residual codec, and exact byte packing unchanged; the downstream LongBench and NIAH gains should return toward the global-profile ByteLadder or uniform-format ProMixed baseline, while an oracle task-category profile should recover most of the gain as a positive control.
compute_budget: Approximately 42 GPU-days on 80GB-class A100/H100 GPUs (about 24 for offline promotion profiling and 18 for held-out LongBench/NIAH serving, baselines, controls, and two implementation iterations) + $0 paid API inference; comfortable within the stated ~150 GPU-day and ~$10k envelope.

differentiation_from_lit.delta: DynamicKV periodically renormalizes layer-specific retained-token counts from prefill attention under a token budget, whereas ByteLadder allocates independently addressable precision residuals and omission at 16-token block granularity under allocator-measured bytes, conditioned by profiles learned with entire task categories held out.

Oaken calibrates data-agnostic outlier thresholds offline and selects quantization scales online inside a fixed low-bit hardware format, whereas ByteLadder retrieves a request-conditioned layer-by-rung promotion table and chooses how many residual segments each block receives.

Ecco fixes a 64-byte compressed block and power-of-two compression ratio with shared k-means and Huffman structures, whereas ByteLadder exposes fixed-width residual segments as separately allocatable units so a request can mix omit, P4, P8, and P16 modes without exceeding its exact byte ceiling.

ChunkKV changes the pruning unit to semantic chunks and reuses selected indices across layers but still makes retain-or-drop decisions under one representation, while ByteLadder keeps the existing ProMixed block unit and promotes block representations to different precision prefixes.

what_step_was_missed: Oaken would have needed to replace its fixed online-offline low-bit format with independently addressable successive-residual segments and bind their per-request promotion order to a held-out-task profile retrieved from prompt-specific GQA evidence.
